What's that one thing that really scared or creeped you out when you were a kid?

Sleep Paralysis. It's been a condition of mine since I was about 6 or 7, didn't figure out that it was medical until I was about 16.

Tl:Dr for Wikipage: Basically when you're mind goes into REM sleep it paralyses your body so you don't act out your dreams. However, in some cases, this will happen before you're actually asleep and you will start to dream/have hallucinations, normally of really scary shit, while you're still wide awake and can't move.
Candyman I couldn't take a shit without thinking this asshole was going to jump through the mirror and shank me.
I ignored the link and then thought a sphincter was going to attack you to save its buddy from your torture.
Bloody Mary still fucking creeps the fuck out of me. Just typing this gives me tingles.
The usual. Dead people, skeletons, aliens, ghosts. Also Big Bird. Strikes me as a pedophile.

The delirium tremens sequence from dumbo. Watched it again as an adult, still fucked up.

http://youtu.be/RoysQe-2HS4
Even though it's meant to scare kids from alchohol, I had to drink as an adult to get over it.

Dad was scrolling through channels while I was like 10. He stopped at a random channel with what something like CSI but obviously a little less child friendly (CSI is oddly kid-friendly minus the sex and some blood). In the next scene, a father gets his neck slit in front of a kid before falling into some hole dug by their captives. It was a terrible scene for a kid that young to see. It's haunted me ever since.
Yeah, people get fucking UP IN ARMS about violence in video games, but I guarantee you can channel surf for 10 minutes and find a tv show on with a grisly murder scene.
I played the shit out of violent video games such as CoD, Battlefield, GTA and Fallout. Nothing was ever as fucked up as that scene and nothing has sat with me more.
The movie Jaws, I saw it when I was 5 and wouldn't swim at the beach for a few years. I still have some psychological issues with swimming at the beach.

My Grandmother had this little wooden girl doll. And for YEARS my uncle would move it around the house without me noticing the initial move. I was dead scared this thing was alive and following me because it always ended up in the same room as me and was going to turn me into a wooden boy

My stepdad showed me the movie Poltergeist when i was like 7 or 8. For nearly a decade afterwards, I was terrified of going to sleep with my closet doors open. I didn't want to meet the same fate as that little girl when she got sucked into her closet! I'm over it now, but god damn was I irrationally scared of open closets when I was younger.

My grandmother let me watch Poltergeist at about 5. The clown doll haunted my nightmares for most of my childhood, and I still can not stand clowns. I managed to watch the remake of Poltergeist with my boyfriend, but he kindly covered my eyes in the clown scenes.
I still don't go to sleep with my closet doors open.
MJ's Thriller music video. Ruined a few nights sleep. Also, the original Jurassic Park. Nightmares galore.
I was a weird kid but i read about lucid dreams one day and they scared the crap out of me. I always tried to have one but would wimp out at the last minute.

I used to have reoccuring nightmares of guys in a van trying to abduct me. I'd always wake up right when they'd pull me in.

My first lucid dream was when I was like "This is that dream again! I should stop running and not be scared, because this isn't real - but what if it isn't a dream?" It was around that time that I stopped having that nightmare.

I found it hard to sleep at night. My little sister had long blonde hair, there was a huge tree outside the window and my dad would fall asleep with the tv on, that 2 am hiss. Guess what movie i was way too young to watch. Oh and Daleks.
Daleks for me too. I used to hide behind the sofa when they came out.

When i was younger (11'ish), there was a house that had a creepy shed next to it. Was told that there was a witch that was kept in there. I was walking home one early evening next to that house. And heard.. "Heeeelp meee".. I nearly crapped my pant and took off running.. Found out later it was a family member that they kept locked up. I feel really bad now, because it was just a wooden tool shed, they kept padlocked. I could have saved her from that, but I just ran away and never went that way again.

Um.....the guy on the neighborhood watch sign...

Shut up, he was creepy, okay?!

I always thought the Block Parent sign was creepy. I also thought they weren't real until I moved into my grandpas house in the nice neighbourhood (so pretty much the last place you'd need a thing like that) and a neighbour up the street had the Block Parent sign in her window.

Mirrors. I was always afraid that my reflection would start doing something different than me, or that someone would appear in the mirror that wasn't in the room.

Okay, I admit - this creeps me out as an adult, too. I have rejected apartments when renting simply because they had mirrored closet doors.

When I was very young: squirrels. Then my parents got me a stuffed animal one and of course they then became adorable.

When I was young: the library ghost from Ghostbusters kept me up a little. I trained my brain to make it funny. Also, The Birds, which my mum thought was an okay Hitchcock film for a young kid. Too much eyeball horror for me at that age.

Beyond that, throughout my childhood I had a lot of recurring nightmares that sometimes made sleep frightening. Worst ones:

-I'd be trying to get to sleep in my bed, tossing and turning, when the hallway light would come on. I'd see one of my sisters come out of the bathroom just outside my door, facing away from me. They'd stand there for a little bit, stone still, and then turn to me, and their face would be just one giant, lipless mouth filled with needle-like teeth. The air would turn solid and the thing would run and grab me.

-I'd be doing something normal, like reading a book in the living room. Nothing would seem out of place. Then a shadowy arm would dart out from underneath something, grab my ankle, and pull me inexorably to the ground. This one happened for a few years off and on until I killed the thing in my dream with my stuffed dog. Thanks, protection/comfort symbols!
ET. The way he looked didn't get to me as much as that first scream noise he made.

The possibility of some creeper pulling me into their van and abducting me.

The 1980s were some interesting times. Between the Cold War and Stranger Danger, I'm surprised any of us survived!
Aliens and the Chupacabra... I was an odd kid, and Unsolved Mysteries fueled all of my deepest childhood fears.

I was 6 when my dad bought some particularly grotesque, rubber Halloween mask. I was playing in the backyard and he just peeked his head over top of the fence and waited.

Using the same mask, I watched him wake my sister while wearing it and kneeling next to her bed. She was 12 at the time and woke up screaming and crying. I laughed.
Crack houses, especially ones that were completely abandoned with no windows only to see shadows move about the house

There's a part in one of the planet of the apes films, (the old ones) where a character is yelling at the apes for cutting out his friends brain. That shit scared me so bad, I slept with the covers over my head for 4 years. Not exaggerating at all, it was 4 years of hiding my head so the apes wouldn't get my brain. Because blankets protect you from stuff like that.
Parents had the teenage boy across the street babysit me. He put on Poltergeist. I still vividly remember how terrified I was during the maggots scene.

Alright, it seems so pointless, but this menu made me feel like I was going to fall into an abyss. Also, that singing fish thingy that you put on your wall. My dad had to give it to my uncle because I started crying in fear every time it spoke.
That ghostly moaning sounds that toilets make.
I always thought my computer was going to explode in the middle of the night when I was 7. Don't know why but it terrified me.
I saw Jaws when I was really young... and got so scared of water I was even afraid of my waterbed. Even to this day I still cant jump off a boat.
The scene in ghostbusters 2 where the evil slime started oozing out of the bathroom faucet, still haunts me to this day.

The unfinished basement of the house I grew up in, with its damp concrete floors and shadowy corners full of old spider webs, all the exposed rafters and the random creaking noises of the house settling and the furnace clicking and hissing to itself.

I never walked up the basement steps, I always fled up the stairway with a feeling that something was reaching up to clutch my ankles.
Watching "The passion of Christ" when I was a kid messed me up for a bit.

E.T. I used to have nightmares about that little bastard.

My grandma had this life sized doll, I mean it must have been at least 4 feet tall, and it would always just be sitting in the living room for everyone to see. That thing scared the shit out of me

Hypnagogia, especially after a nightmare or night terrors. I never did experience sleep paralysis as far as I know; but I've experienced a full range of hallucinations relating to going into and coming out of sleep. The half-way world was much like reality, only with this overarching feeling of misery and terror. It was like being hunted by ghosts and knowing there wasn't anything you could do.
